key_insight: OmniRay aims to reconstruct 3D scenes from a single image without assuming a pinhole camera. Its central idea is to represent camera geometry with composite ray fields that reflect both overall projection and finer variations.
problem_solved: Monocular reconstruction models built around pinhole cameras can distort geometry in fisheye and panoramic images. Existing camera-aware approaches use a single fixed basis to represent camera geometry at different levels of detail.
method: Represent camera geometry through per-pixel viewing rays rather than a fixed pinhole model.
Treat camera geometry as hierarchical, motivating composite ray fields instead of one fixed basis.
Target camera-agnostic monocular 3D reconstruction; the supplied abstract is truncated before implementation and evaluation details.
impact: This approach could make single-image 3D reconstruction more useful across cameras with different lens projections, especially wide-angle systems. Performance improvements cannot be assessed from the supplied excerpt.
visual_elements: Side-by-side pinhole, fisheye, and panoramic images with viewing-ray overlays.
A hierarchy diagram showing overall camera projection and finer ray-field variations.
A pipeline diagram: single image → composite ray field → reconstructed 3D scene.
A conceptual comparison illustrating distortion from a mismatched camera assumption.
paper_title: OmniRay: Camera-Agnostic Monocular 3D Reconstruction with Composite Ray Fields
paper_authors: Namitha Guruprasad, Abhay Yadav, Cheng Peng, Rama Chellappa, Anand Bhattad
